chapter: Ben Webster, Tatum and Los Angeles scene
title: Central Avenue and Watts clubs, mixed audiences
summary: He describes the mixed audiences and after-hours clubs of Central Avenue, where he met Earl Hines and Barney Kessel.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: No, but I was thinking of the Central Avenue scene when you first hit here, that was just around the time when the War started and all that. And I guess the audience in those clubs was mixed. Or was it mostly a Black audience?
It was all mixed up, yeah. This was... I got down there in '40. When was Pearl Harbor? '42?
December of '41.
It didn't even happen then. It didn't happen until after the War, is when all this race stuff started.
Because in New York on 52nd Street, there used to be
Rowles - 35
little problems with soldiers on leave who might from Down South and stuff, and they would go on the Street and see mixed bands and mixed audiences and so on...
Oh, I see what you're talking about.
...and then they'd get a little drunk, and then there might be some problems there.

There might have been. Because I wasn't up around Watts and Central during those days too much. But all the time I ever was ever up around there, there was never any trouble. Never. But I wouldn't go there now. I wouldn't go near the place.
Nothing much happening musically any more there.
No. That's the first time I ever saw Earl Hines, up there. I met Barney Kessel up there when he came to town.
Barney was from...
Oklahoma.
Oklahoma, right.
Yeah. I used to hang around up there. To go up there, it was just like walking out on the street here. Nothin' to it.
A lot of joints?
Oh yeah.
After-hours?
Rowles - 36
All kinds of after-hour places. Brothers was the name of one place, in a house. But it was a nightclub.
